findings.reason: The protected implementation evaluates N-ary tree diameter iteratively by collecting nodes in parent-first order using an explicit stack, then processing in reverse postorder to compute downward heights and candidate path lengths (longest + second_longest child heights). This avoids recursion call-stack overflows for deep trees while maintaining O(N) time and O(N) space; no candidate is required.

The iterative reverse postorder guarantees all child heights are calculated before evaluating the parent. For each node, finding the two largest child downward branch lengths calculates the longest simple path whose peak is that node. Maximizing longest + second over all nodes correctly considers all potential diameter paths.
Traversing N nodes and N-1 total child edges twice takes O(N) time. The ordering list, stack, and height map use O(N) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts an N-ary tree root Node, handles single-node trees (returning diameter 0), linear chains, and wide star trees correctly, and returns the maximum edge count.

The approach accurately details summarizing subtrees by downward height, iterative postorder evaluation without call-stack recursion, and O(N) time/space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover two-pass graph sweeps, all-pairs searches, recursive DFS, single nodes, chains, wide stars, and single-child nodes.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the exact same iterative reverse postorder height-combination algorithm with SHA-256 digests dd954fca6db7d69bfcf7a89b823033a1343d9b34888253080f702be29ecc543c and 407cfcb27ecfc135046a9432e68df988b59fd51f3b3775d09b18874211810e5c.
